mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive quarters of GDP decline, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which leads to increased corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 2% in a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the same period, it signals robust economic demand, leading to increased corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST increases > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between GDPC1 growth, HOUST increase, and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, leading to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between FEDFUNDS level, CPIAUCSL increase, and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of periods following three consecutive months of PAYEMS increase, or the correlation between PAYEMS increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
